root_cause.text: The iomap_read_folio_iter() function failed to invalidate ctx->cur_folio when submitting partial folio IO without an ifs (iomap_folio_state) structure, causing the folio to be accessed by both the IO helper and iomap_read_end(), resulting in a use-after-free condition.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that the original condition `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len)` only cleared ctx->cur_folio when the entire folio was submitted for IO. However, when i_blkbits differs from IO granularity and no ifs is allocated, IO can be submitted for less than the full folio size. In this case, the condition would not trigger, leaving ctx->cur_folio pointing to the folio even though the IO helper owns it and will complete the read. The fix adds `|| !ifs` to the condition to unconditionally invalidate ctx->cur_folio when there is no ifs attached, preventing double-access to the folio.

intent_record.intent_summary: Declare iomap_folio_state pointer variable to support upcoming folio state operations in the read path.
intent_record.what: Added a new variable declaration `struct iomap_folio_state *ifs;` in the iomap_read_folio_iter function's local variable block.
intent_record.how: This declares an uninitialized pointer variable that will be used later in the function to reference iomap folio state structures. The variable is now available for subsequent code to assign and use, enabling operations on folio state metadata.

intent_record.intent_summary: Capture the return value from ifs_alloc() to enable proper use of the allocated inode folio state structure in subsequent code.
intent_record.what: Changed the statement `ifs_alloc(iter->inode, folio, iter->flags);` to assign its return value to variable `ifs` with `ifs = ifs_alloc(iter->inode, folio, iter->flags);`
intent_record.how: The function call to `ifs_alloc()` now captures and stores its return value in the `ifs` variable instead of discarding it. This enables subsequent code to use the allocated structure pointer for further operations, whereas previously the return value was ignored.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix folio ownership handoff to IO helper when no ifs is attached, preventing stalls with smaller IO granularity filesystems.
intent_record.what: Modified the condition for clearing ctx->cur_folio from checking only if all bytes are submitted (*bytes_submitted == folio_len) to also checking if ifs is NULL (!ifs). Updated the preceding comment to explain both conditions: folio ownership is handed to the IO helper when either the entire folio is submitted OR there is no ifs attached.
intent_record.how: This change allows the folio ownership to be released to the IO helper in an additional scenario: when there are no io_folio_state structures attached to the folio, even if not all bytes have been submitted. This prevents the code from getting stuck waiting for completion when a filesystem or block device uses smaller IO granularity than the folio size, ensuring proper folio lifecycle management in such cases.

relevance_review.reason: This group only declares a pointer variable for future use. It does not address the core vulnerability issue, which is the failure to invalidate ctx->cur_folio when submitting partial folio IO without an ifs structure. A variable declaration alone does not fix the use-after-free condition caused by concurrent access to the folio.

The group captures the return value from ifs_alloc() for proper use of the allocated structure. However, the vulnerability root cause is about failing to invalidate ctx->cur_folio when submitting partial folio IO *without* an ifs structure (i.e., when ifs is not allocated or is NULL). This group addresses proper handling when ifs *is* successfully allocated, which is orthogonal to the core issue of missing invalidation in the no-ifs case.

The group directly addresses the root cause by fixing the folio ownership handoff when no ifs (iomap_folio_state) is attached. The vulnerability occurred because ctx->cur_folio was not invalidated when submitting partial folio IO without an ifs structure, causing concurrent access. This fix ensures proper ownership transfer to the IO helper, preventing the use-after-free condition described in the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This condition only invalidates ctx->cur_folio when the ENTIRE folio has been submitted (*bytes_submitted == folio_len). However, when submitting partial folio IO without an ifs structure, the folio can still be accessed by both the IO helper and iomap_read_end() even when only a portion is submitted, causing a use-after-free. The condition should also invalidate ctx->cur_folio for partial submissions when no ifs is attached.

However, when submitting partial folio IO without an ifs (iomap_folio_state) structure, the folio can still be accessed by both the IO helper and iomap_read_end() even when only a portion is submitted. This condition fails to account for the case where partial folio IO is submitted without ifs, allowing concurrent access to the folio and causing a use-after-free condition.

The vulnerability manifests because ctx->cur_folio is not invalidated for partial folio IO submissions without ifs, allowing the folio to be accessed by both the IO helper and iomap_read_end() after the partial submission, resulting in use-after-free. The statement itself is correct, but its conditional guard is insufficient.

Author: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit IS the fix itself. The diff shows the corrective changes made to address the vulnerability. The key fixes are: (1) At lines 545-551, when bytes_submitted equals folio_len (entire folio read by IO helper), ctx->cur_folio is set to NULL to invalidate it, preventing subsequent access. (2) At lines 578-579, iomap_read_end() is now only called if ctx->cur_folio is not NULL, preventing access to a folio that the IO helper has already taken ownership of. (3) The +1 bias in iomap_read_init() (line 424) and iomap_read_end() (line 480) has been removed since the folio invalidation now prevents the use-after-free. (4) The condition at line 478 changed from 'else if (!bytes_submitted)' to 'else' with a WARN_ON_ONCE check, ensuring proper handling of the no-ifs case. These changes directly address the root cause: preventing access to ctx->cur_folio after it has been submitted to the IO helper without an ifs structure.
